domain.description: How to design, implement, and evaluate memory and knowledge systems: RAG, embeddings, vector stores, chunking, hybrid search, reranking, grounding, deduplication, contradiction detection, memory promotion/rejection, privacy governance, and long-term agent memory.

taxonomy.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
taxonomy.description: Combining retrieval with generation to ground outputs in external knowledge.

taxonomy.name: Semantic Memory Architecture
taxonomy.description: Structured long-term factual memory with embeddings and indexing.

taxonomy.name: Episodic Memory Architecture
taxonomy.description: Session-level, time-ordered event memory for context continuity.

taxonomy.name: Vector Embeddings
taxonomy.description: Dense vector representations of text, code, or structured data for similarity search.

taxonomy.name: Vector Stores and FAISS
taxonomy.description: Index structures (FAISS, Annoy, HNSW) for efficient nearest-neighbor search.

taxonomy.name: Chunking and Document Segmentation
taxonomy.description: Splitting documents into retrieval units while preserving coherence.

taxonomy.name: Metadata Design
taxonomy.description: Attaching structured metadata to chunks for filtering, ranking, and provenance.

taxonomy.name: Hybrid Search
taxonomy.description: Combining dense vector search with sparse lexical or keyword search.

taxonomy.name: Reranking
taxonomy.description: Second-stage scoring to improve top-k relevance after initial retrieval.

taxonomy.name: Context Compression
taxonomy.description: Reducing retrieved content size to fit context windows without losing salience.

taxonomy.name: Grounding and Citation
taxonomy.description: Linking generated content back to specific retrieved sources.

taxonomy.name: Deduplication
taxonomy.description: Detecting and removing redundant or near-duplicate memory records.

taxonomy.name: Contradiction Detection
taxonomy.description: Identifying conflicting information across retrieved or stored records.

taxonomy.name: Memory Promotion / Rejection
taxonomy.description: Deciding which memories enter long-term storage and which are discarded.

taxonomy.name: Memory Decay / Update Policy
taxonomy.description: Rules for aging, refreshing, or evicting memories over time.

taxonomy.name: Retrieval Evaluation
taxonomy.description: Measuring precision, recall, MRR, nDCG, and ranking stability.

taxonomy.name: Knowledge Graph Integration
taxonomy.description: Combining vector retrieval with structured graph traversal for multi-hop reasoning.

taxonomy.name: Privacy and Memory Governance
taxonomy.description: Ensuring sensitive data is not leaked through retrieval or stored inappropriately.

taxonomy.name: Local-First Memory Design
taxonomy.description: Architecting memory to run on-device without external cloud dependencies.

taxonomy.name: Long-Term Agent Memory
taxonomy.description: Persistent memory across sessions, tasks, and restarts for autonomous agents.

acceptance_criteria.description: A source is accepted only if it is safe, attributable, technically relevant, and cross-checkable.
minimum_conditions: Relevance to at least one taxonomy category
Not contradicted by a more authoritative source
No critical risk flagged by safety rubric
acceptance_criteria.decision_rule: Accept if score >= 55 and no critical risks; hold if 40-54 or incomplete; reject if < 40 or any critical risk.

rejection_criteria.description: Automatic rejection conditions regardless of popularity.
critical_risks: Source requires copying full copyrighted text to be useful
Abandoned and directly contradicted by a newer official source

dimensions.attribution_quality: Can the source be clearly attributed to known authors, orgs, or maintainers?
dimensions.primary_source_quality: Is this a primary source (paper, official repo, official docs) rather than repackaged blog?
dimensions.technical_depth: Does the source contain concrete architecture, algorithms, or implementation details?
dimensions.implementation_relevance: Can the ideas be implemented or adapted without vendor-specific proprietary infrastructure?
dimensions.retrieval_method_clarity: Are retrieval steps, indexing choices, and query paths clearly defined?
dimensions.memory_architecture_clarity: Is the memory structure (short-term, long-term, episodic, semantic) explicitly described?
dimensions.reproducibility: Are there reproducible steps, examples, or tests?
dimensions.license_clarity: Is the license clearly stated and compatible with metadata reference?
dimensions.maintenance_status: Is the repo/docs actively maintained, or at least archived with clear status?
dimensions.test_or_example_presence: Does the source include runnable examples, tests, or demos?
dimensions.copyright_safety: Can we reference it at metadata/summary level without copyright risk?
dimensions.relevance_to_brain: Does it map directly to a Brain memory/RAG capability target?
dimensions.risk_of_hype_or_marketing: Is the content free of exaggerated marketing claims? (5 = very safe, 0 = pure hype)
dimensions.risk_of_obsolescence: Is the source likely to remain relevant for 12+ months?
dimensions.risk_of_vendor_lock_in: Does the approach require a specific vendor/cloud service? (5 = vendor-neutral, 0 = full lock-in)
dimensions.risk_of_privacy_leakage: Does the design risk leaking private or sensitive data? (5 = very safe, 0 = high risk)
dimensions.risk_of_unverifiable_claims: Are core claims supported by evidence, code, or reproducible results?

contrast_rubric.description: Each candidate source must be contrasted against at least two sources of different types when possible.
contrast_types: vector DB docs vs FAISS docs
RAG framework docs vs RAG evaluation framework
memory paper vs agent memory implementation
long-term memory claim vs reproducible implementation

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
sources.authors_or_org: Lewis et al. / Facebook AI / UCL / others
sources.expected_learning_value: Foundational RAG architecture: pre-trained retriever + seq2seq generator, with end-to-end fine-tuning.
sources.notes: Seminal RAG paper. Well-cited. Architecture is concise and reproducible.

sources.title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
sources.expected_learning_value: Pre-training with a differentiable retriever, showing retrieval improves knowledge-intensive tasks.
sources.notes: Early influential work on learned retrievers. Less directly applicable than RAG but historically important.

sources.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
sources.expected_learning_value: Dual-encoder architecture for dense passage retrieval, outperforming BM25 on many QA tasks.
sources.notes: Open-source implementation available. Strong empirical results. Widely adopted.

sources.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
sources.expected_learning_value: Late-interaction architecture that balances efficiency and effectiveness for passage retrieval.
sources.notes: Very active repo. Good for understanding reranking trade-offs.

sources.title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
sources.expected_learning_value: Hypothetical Document Embedding (HyDE) generates pseudo-documents to improve zero-shot retrieval.
sources.notes: Simple and effective idea. Risk: generated pseudo-docs may introduce hallucinated queries.

sources.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
sources.authors_or_org: Asai et al. / University of Washington / others
sources.expected_learning_value: On-demand retrieval with self-reflection tokens: retrieve only when needed and critique retrieved content.
sources.notes: Active repo. Strong idea for avoiding unnecessary retrieval and improving grounding.

sources.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
sources.authors_or_org: Packer et al. / UC Berkeley / others
sources.expected_learning_value: Virtual context management inspired by OS paging: moving data between context and external memory.
sources.notes: Very active. Now branded as Letta. Strong for long-term agent memory design.

sources.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
sources.expected_learning_value: Memory stream + reflection + planning creates believable long-horizon agent behavior.
sources.notes: Repo available and MIT-licensed. Good for cross-checking implementation of memory architecture.

sources.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
sources.expected_learning_value: Building a knowledge graph from source documents improves global reasoning and summarization over vector-only RAG.
sources.notes: Microsoft Research. Graph + vector hybrid is increasingly relevant for complex reasoning.

sources.title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval
sources.expected_learning_value: Hierarchical tree retrieval by recursively summarizing chunks, enabling multi-scale context.
sources.notes: Active repo. Good for chunking and hierarchical memory design.

sources.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
sources.expected_learning_value: LLMs perform best when relevant information is at the beginning or end of context; middle positions degrade performance.
sources.notes: Critical finding for RAG context placement. High citation count.

sources.title: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
sources.authors_or_org: Muennighoff et al. / Hugging Face / others
sources.expected_learning_value: Standardized benchmark for comparing embedding models across dozens of tasks and languages.
sources.notes: Very active. Leaderboard widely used. Good for embedding model selection.

sources.title: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-Shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models
sources.expected_learning_value: Diverse IR benchmark for zero-shot evaluation of dense, sparse, and hybrid retrievers.
sources.notes: Widely adopted for IR evaluation. Good coverage of domains and tasks.

sources.title: FAISS -- A Library for Efficient Similarity Search and Clustering of Dense Vectors
sources.expected_learning_value: Production-grade nearest-neighbor search with GPU support, quantization, and multiple index types.
sources.notes: Brain already uses FAISS. Official docs are the primary source for index tuning.

sources.title: LangChain Documentation -- Retrieval and Memory
sources.expected_learning_value: Composable RAG pipelines, chunking strategies, metadata enrichment, and memory integrations.
sources.notes: Mature ecosystem. Some API churn. Good reference for chunking and metadata patterns.

sources.title: LangGraph Memory and Checkpointing Documentation
sources.expected_learning_value: Stateful graph execution with short-term and long-term memory, checkpoints, and human-in-the-loop.
sources.notes: Good for understanding stateful memory in agent workflows. Active development.

sources.title: LlamaIndex -- Data Framework for LLM Applications
sources.expected_learning_value: Advanced indexing, query engines, and agentic RAG with multi-hop reasoning and knowledge graphs.
sources.notes: Very active. Good for advanced RAG patterns. Some features require external APIs.

sources.title: Chroma -- AI-Native Open-Source Embedding Database
sources.expected_learning_value: Developer-friendly vector database with local-first deployment and easy embedding integration.
sources.notes: Local-first is good for Brain's privacy requirements. Less scalable than FAISS for very large indices.

sources.title: Qdrant -- Vector Database Documentation
sources.expected_learning_value: Open-source vector database with filtering, hybrid search, and quantization.
sources.notes: Good hybrid search features. Self-hostable. Alternative to FAISS for some use cases.

sources.title: Weaviate -- Vector Search Engine Documentation
sources.expected_learning_value: Vector search with GraphQL interface, modular AI integrations, and knowledge graph features.
sources.notes: Good for graph + vector hybrid. GraphQL dependency adds complexity. Some features are cloud-only.

sources.title: Pinecone -- Managed Vector Database (Vendor Reference)
sources.expected_learning_value: Reference for managed vector DB features: metadata filtering, hybrid search, sparse-dense vectors.
sources.notes: Proprietary managed service. High vendor lock-in. Useful as a feature reference but not for Brain's local-first design.

sources.title: RAGAS -- Retrieval-Augmented Generation Assessment
sources.expected_learning_value: Metrics for evaluating RAG: faithfulness, answer relevance, context precision, context recall.
sources.notes: Very active. Well-documented. Good for Brain's retrieval evaluation needs.

sources.title: DeepEval RAG Metrics Documentation
sources.expected_learning_value: RAG-specific metrics (contextual relevance, faithfulness, answer relevancy) with CI/CD integration.
sources.notes: Good for automated RAG evaluation. Some metrics depend on external LLM APIs.

sources.title: TruLens -- Explainable AI and LLM Evaluation
sources.expected_learning_value: Instrumentation for tracing, evaluating, and explaining LLM/RAG application behavior.
sources.notes: Good for observability + evaluation. Enterprise backing. Useful for privacy governance patterns.

sources.title: Microsoft GraphRAG -- A Modular Graph-Based RAG System
sources.expected_learning_value: Open-source implementation of GraphRAG: building knowledge graphs from documents for multi-hop reasoning.
sources.notes: Active Microsoft repo. Good for understanding graph + vector hybrid RAG. Self-hostable.

sources.title: Letta (formerly MemGPT) -- Memory Management for LLM Agents
sources.expected_learning_value: Virtual context management with memory tiers, agent personas, and multi-user support.
sources.notes: Rebranded from MemGPT to Letta. Very active. Good for long-term memory architecture patterns.

sources.title: LangSmith Dataset and Evaluation Documentation
sources.expected_learning_value: Hosted platform for dataset management, online/offline evaluation, and trace comparison.
sources.notes: Proprietary platform. High vendor lock-in. Useful as a reference for evaluation workflow design but not for Brain's local-first architecture.

sources.title: Top 10 Vector Databases You Must Use -- Unattributed Blog
sources.expected_learning_value: Generic listicle. No architecture depth.
sources.notes: No attribution. No evidence. SEO content. Reject.

cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: Retriever + generator pipeline is the foundational RAG architecture.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: LangChain provides composable implementations of chunking, embedding, and retrieval patterns described in the RAG paper.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: How does LangChain's default chunking compare to the optimal chunking for a given corpus?

cross_source_contrast_matrix.contrast_type: vector DB docs vs vector DB repo
cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: Both provide local-first vector search with metadata filtering.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: FAISS is lower-level and more scalable; Chroma is higher-level and more developer-friendly.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: At what index size does FAISS significantly outperform Chroma?

cross_source_contrast_matrix.contrast_type: RAG eval framework vs RAG eval framework docs
cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: Automated RAG evaluation requires faithfulness, relevance, and context precision metrics.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: RAGAS focuses on metric definitions; DeepEval focuses on CI/CD integration and test case management.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: Which framework's metrics are less prone to LLM judge bias?

cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: Virtual context management with memory tiers improves long-horizon agent performance.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: Repo adds multi-user support, REST API, and persistence backends not in the paper.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: How does MemGPT/Letta handle memory fragmentation over very long sessions?

cross_source_contrast_matrix.contrast_type: dense retrieval paper vs late-interaction paper
cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: Dense retrieval outperforms sparse BM25 on many tasks.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: DPR is more efficient at scale; ColBERT is more effective per query but more compute-intensive.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: Can ColBERT's late interaction be approximated to match DPR's latency?

cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: Knowledge graphs improve global reasoning over vector-only RAG.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: Repo provides the actual indexing pipeline, query engine, and configuration.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: How does GraphRAG perform on small corpora where graph structure is sparse?

cross_source_contrast_matrix.contrast_type: context placement paper vs hierarchical retrieval paper
cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: Context window usage is critical for RAG performance.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: Lost in the Middle warns about position bias; RAPTOR addresses it by hierarchical summarization.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: Does RAPTOR's tree structure fully mitigate the middle-position degradation?

cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: Standardized benchmarks are essential for comparing retrieval and embedding quality.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: MTEB focuses on embedding model quality across tasks; BEIR focuses on zero-shot retrieval system quality.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: Which benchmark better predicts real-world RAG performance?

cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: Both provide vector search with metadata filtering.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.contradicts: Pinecone is proprietary and cloud-only; FAISS is open-source and local.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: Pinecone is easier to deploy at scale; FAISS is free and fully controllable.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: What is the total cost of ownership for Pinecone vs. self-hosted FAISS at Brain's scale?

knowledge_record_schema.description: Schema for a future knowledge record if ingestion is ever authorized.
knowledge_record_schema.retention_policy: Metadata and summary only. Full content must remain external.
